memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against anyone among your people, but love your neighbour as yourself. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 19:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here it is — one of the most famous sentences ever written, sitting quietly in the middle of Leviticus between laws about gossip and laws about crossbreeding cattle.

Jesus lifted this verse out and placed it at the summit of everything. Asked which commandment was greatest, He named love for God first, and then said: And the second is like it: Love your neighbour as yourself. All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments (Matt 22:39-40).

Everything hangs here.

Notice what comes first in the verse, though. Before "love your neighbour" comes do not seek revenge or bear a grudge. Love is not only what we do; it is what we refuse to keep doing. Refusing to settle the score. Refusing to nurse the grievance we have every right to hold.

A grudge feels like power over someone. It is actually a weight we carry on their behalf.

And as yourself is the measure. Not sentimentally, but practically — with the same instinctive attention you give your own needs. You do not have to work up warm feelings towards yourself. You simply act in your own interest without thinking. Do that for someone else.

Then Jesus went further still: love one another. As I have loved you (John 13:34).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What grudge are you carrying that is costing you more than them?
2. What would it look like to treat one person's needs as instinctively as your own?
3. Who is the neighbour God has put in front of you this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, free me from grudges I have every right to hold. Teach me to love my neighbour with the same instinctive care I give myself, as Christ has loved me. Amen.
